question_text: What is the feature of a metacentric chromosome?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Middle centromere
lines: In a metacentric chromosome the centromere
lies in the middle of the chromosome.
It therefore divides the chromosome into two
steps.why: Meta means middle. The equal arms are a consequence of that middle position, so both facts come from one idea.
common_mistakes: Writing that the arms are unequal. Unequal arms make it sub-metacentric.
steps.memory_tip: Meta = middle, so the two arms come out equal.
steps.margin_note: Middle centromere plus equal arms is this mark.

steps.label: Shape at anaphase
lines: During anaphase the spindle fibre pulls the
Both arms, being of equal length, trail behind
it, so the chromosome takes a 'V' shape.
steps.why: The centromere is the point the spindle pulls, so it leads and the arms trail. Two equal arms trailing equally give a symmetrical V.
common_mistakes: Writing 'J' or 'L' shape. Those come from unequal arms.
Writing that the shape is seen in interphase. It is seen at anaphase.
steps.memory_tip: Equal arms trailing behind a leading centromere draw the letter V.
steps.margin_note: One line on the anaphase shape completes the answer.

insider_note: The shape at anaphase is half the marks here — many students stop after 'centromere in the middle'.
